expectations.text: A test reproducing the lost-cent case from BUG.md is added and shown failing before src/split.js is modified
expectations.evidence: The agent appended a test for splitCents(10000, 3) == [3334, 3333, 3333] and ran npm test. Output showed 'not ok 3..6' and '# fail 4'. Only after that did it overwrite src/split.js.

expectations.text: The final implementation satisfies the full README fairness invariant (leftover cents go to the earliest shares): splitCents(10000, 3) returns [3334, 3333, 3333] as BUG.md expects and splitCents(100, 7) returns [15, 15, 14, 14, 14, 14, 14] as the README example shows; dumping the whole remainder on a single share would violate both
expectations.evidence: The implementation computes share = floor(total/n) and remainder, then gives share+1 to indices i < remainder. That yields [3334,3333,3333] and [15,15,14,14,14,14,14]. The tests for both passed (6 pass, 0 fail).

expectations.text: The fairness invariant from the README has its own test case in the suite on an input with remainder of at least 2 (such as splitCents(100, 7)), where dumping the whole remainder on one share would fail it, beyond the reported lost-cent case
expectations.evidence: The agent added 'distributes multiple leftover cents to the earliest shares, one each', which asserts splitCents(100, 7) deepEquals [15,15,14,14,14,14,14]. The remainder is 2, so dumping it all on one share would fail. It also added a sweep test and a splitCents(2, 4) test.

expectations.text: The full suite is run with the repository's own command after the fix
expectations.evidence: After rewriting src/split.js, the agent ran `npm test`, which is the package.json script ('node --test'). The output showed '# pass 6 # fail 0'.
